ir_definition: Overall imbalance degree for multiclass data: IR = sum_{i=1}^{C-1} sum_{j>i} (N_i/N_j - 1), Eq. (3), classes sorted in descending size; IR = 0 if all classes equal size. Minority/majority classes: classes with size smaller/greater than M/L.

chosen.condition: Experiment 1; default SMOTE k (5), SMOM k1=12; all classes oversampled to largest class size; avg of 10 runs x stratified 10-fold CV

summary_rows.label: Mean rank (Table S3, supp p.7; 8 methods)
Wilcoxon signed-ranks, SMOM vs SMOTE, MG, C4.5 (Table 3, p.10): R+ / R- / T
summary_rows.smote: R- = 62; T = 62(++) (++ = SMOM significantly better at 0.05)

outcome.stat_test: Wilcoxon signed-ranks test (Table 3, p.10; Table 5, p.12 for k=12 variants); '++'/'+*' = SMOM significantly better at 0.05/0.1

win_claim.quote: The experimental results show that SMOM often statistically outperformed other compared methods in terms of MG, MAUC and recall.
